ticket.title: Add the repository to the telemetry span contract
ticket.description: TelemetrySpan carries span_id, trace_id, parent_span_id, binary, command, task_key, branch, status, started_at_ms, duration_ms and first_diagnostic, and no repository. Federation encoded ownership in the log path, so rooting telemetry at the suite deletes that encoding: one log could no longer say which repository a miter run touched, and branch does not disambiguate two worktrees on one branch name. Add repo. Also populate task_key where a span is opened: sawhorse completion_span sets command and never task_key, so both spans currently on disk carry neither field and the join to the spool sits at zero coverage. This is a contract change under ADR 0002 and lands before the writer moves.
acceptance_criteria: a span round-trips repo; a span with no repo is legal for a run outside any checkout and the panel groups unknowns explicitly; the two fields are populated by the emitting helper, proven by a test that opens a span with a task key

events.description:
TelemetrySpan carries span_id, trace_id, parent_span_id, binary, command, task_key, branch, status, started_at_ms, duration_ms and first_diagnostic, and no repository. Federation encoded ownership in the log path, so rooting telemetry at the suite deletes that encoding: one log could no longer say which repository a miter run touched, and branch does not disambiguate two worktrees on one branch name. Add repo. Also populate task_key where a span is opened: sawhorse completion_span sets command and never task_key, so both spans currently on disk carry neither field and the join to the spool sits at zero coverage. This is a contract change under ADR 0002 and lands before the writer moves.

DONE 2026-11-08 (commit 29f9f87, common).

TelemetrySpan carries repo: Option<String>, omitted when absent. Two tests: a span with a repository round-trips it,
and one without omits the key rather than writing null.

This is the field the unified writer needs: the path used to encode the repository and rooting the writer at the suite
deletes that encoding, so without it a single log cannot answer which repository a miter run touched - and a branch
name does not disambiguate two worktrees on the same branch.

Still owed from the telemetry set: GB-338 (root the writer at the suite, delete the federating reader), GB-339 (one
span per CLI invocation across nine more tools), GB-340 (test runs must not write the production log), GB-341
(retention, configurable and tracked separately from the ephemeral log).
